key_insight: Fewer than 2% of FDA-authorized AI medical devices are prognostic, with prediction horizons spanning minutes to years, highlighting a substantial gap and emerging regulatory/ethical concerns as prognostic tools expand.
problem_solved: Identifies and quantifies the scarcity of prognostic AI devices among FDA approvals and clarifies the regulatory and ethical challenges that must be addressed as prognostic AI becomes more common.
method: Systematic analysis of FDA-authorized AI/ML medical devices to identify and categorize prognostic tools
Characterization of prediction horizons (minutes to years) and mapping of device use-cases
Assessment of regulatory and ethical implications based on device features and existing approval pathways
impact: Alerts AI/ML practitioners and developers that prognostic models are underrepresented in approvals and that design, validation, and deployment must proactively address regulatory pathways and ethical issues (e.g., prognostic uncertainty, patient autonomy, downstream interventions).
visual_elements: Pie chart showing proportion of prognostic vs. non-prognostic FDA-authorized AI devices (<2% slice highlighted)
Histogram or timeline of prediction horizons from minutes to years
Flowchart mapping regulatory checkpoints and ethical considerations for prognostic device approval
Icons representing clinical settings and potential downstream actions (ICU alerts, chronic care planning, preventive interventions)
paper_title: Authorization of prognostic AI medical devices
paper_authors: Urs J. Muehlematter, Kerstin Noelle Vokinger
